:::{#exm-program-as-string}
#### A program file is a description

A Python script saved to disk is a sequence of bytes,
so it is a binary string,
and the Python interpreter reads that string as a program,
much as @def-tm-description reads a string as a [Turing machine](#def-turing-machine).
Appending a comment line to the script gives a longer string
that [describes](#def-tm-description) the same program,
which is the padding convention of @def-tm-description.
A file that is not valid Python makes the interpreter stop with a syntax error,
which plays the role of the fixed machine that invalid strings describe,
for instance one that [halts](#def-turing-machine) at once.

:::
